To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phytochrome degradation can explain the high-irradiance response and that the two-step model is the minimal set of reactions necessary to describe all available data on phytochrome A.

phytochrome is degraded by a two-step process in Arabidopsis, that phytochrome degradation is a major mechanism for the high irradiance responses and that phytochrome sensing of far-red-rich light can be quantitavely explained based exclusively on degradation.
phytochrome degradation is the key to the high irradiance responses of plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism underlying the physiological function of phytochrome in plants.
the question of how phytochromes are able to sense light in a specific way.
the elucidation of molecular mechanisms underlying the high irradiance requirement of phytochrome action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phytochrome A high irradiance response is mediated by the tagging of Pr, which in turn is regulated by Pfr.
phytochrome degradation kinetics and the high irradiation response are tightly coupled.
phytochrome degradation, in addition to light perception, is the key element in the phytochrome signalling chain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phytochrome degradation kinetics are sufficient to account for physiological responses to light.
phytochrome-mediated far-red light responses are based on the unique properties of the phytochrome A protein, namely its high stability and its ability to undergo light-induced degradation.

phytochrome-mediated responses to far-red-rich irradiation are the result of an interplay between two opposing mechanisms, activation by red light and degradation by far-red light, and that this interplay is modulated by the light intensity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ability of phytochrome to sense light is a consequence of the ability to sense the light-induced degradation of the protein.
phytochrome degradation can account for the entire physiological response to light in Arabidopsis.
the high irradiance responses of Arabidopsis phytochrome A to far-red light can be explained quantitatively on the basis of a model of phytochrome degradation.
